# AiBTC
AiBTC is a Bitcoin Hybrid DEX and fair-launch trading platform, powered by the AIBRC protocol. @ is both identity and address. Through @, AiBTC lets AI understand Bitcoin and makes every Bitcoin asset programmable. AIBRC, BRC-20, Runes and EVM assets all live in 1 address, with 1 fair launch. 1 liquidity pool powers 2 Swaps: 0-gas Instant Swap and Bitcoin Block Swap. AiBTC brings public-chain-grade trading and fair launches to Bitcoin.

Atom Unit: reserves, deposits and withdrawals
AiBTC reserves follow the atomic unit model of the Atom Unit Protocol, and users and their Agents can verify their own on-chain reserves. Instant Swap uses the available account balance; Block Swap pays BTC directly from the wallet, with no deposit first. BTC withdrawal uses mutual signing, and AIBRC withdrawal and Block Swap use co-signing, all through the same Atom Unit.

Atom Unit guide: https://aibtc.io/docs/atom-unit/

One @ connects identity, assets, launches, trading and Agents

AiBTC brings a shared asset standard and a unified account model to Bitcoin, connecting fair launches, markets, liquidity, programmable rules and applications.

@ is both identity and address: a common entry point through which users and Agents understand assets and participate in the ecosystem. AIBRC gives wallets, applications, trading tools and Agents a consistent language for asset identity, balances and interaction rules.

Agents recognize Bitcoin-native AIBRC assets through addresses and balances, without identifying individual asset-carrying UTXOs. Applications can reuse asset lookup, balance queries, allocation logic and transaction-building tools around the same standard.

1 address: an AIBRC address-account foundation connects same-root BRC-20 and Runes branches, EVM rule references and external contract associations. Each asset uses the state, rules and integrations of its corresponding protocol or contract.

1 fair launch: a shared root deployment establishes provenance and connects the root asset, same-root branches, bonding-curve trading and graduation liquidity.

1 liquidity pool, 2 Swaps: the same AIBRC market and liquidity pool serve 0-gas Instant Swap and Bitcoin Block Swap. Instant's 0-gas experience means each account trade runs without a separate Bitcoin network fee; trading fees follow the market's base and covenant rules.

Through AIBRC, Smart Covenant and AIBTC CORE, programmable rules connect asset creation, trading, fee distribution and buybacks. Agents can read those rules, organize user intent and compute results.

Connecting what the Bitcoin ecosystem has built

Ordinals, BRC-20, Runes, Atomicals, RGB++, Taproot Assets, Lightning and L2s have brought different technologies, assets, tools, communities and cultures to Bitcoin.

Each protocol has its own asset rules and integrations. A project expanding into another ecosystem often builds another asset, another market and another pool of liquidity.

AIBRC × AiBTC connects that work through a shared account foundation, reusable tools and same-root provenance. Projects keep the starting points of different protocols while building around an AIBRC root asset and core market. Users gain a consistent entry point, developers reuse common interfaces, and Agents work with explicit asset identities and computable rules.

Let every protocol keep innovating, while the assets, applications and communities built around them remain connected.

Core components

AIBRC: a shared asset and account standard

AIBRC Covenant Inscription identifies protocol accounts by the scriptPubKey of a Bitcoin address and records assets as address-level balances.

Asset operations express addresses, amounts and authorization rules. The model supports balance-based transfers and allocation to multiple addresses in one transaction.

BTC UTXOs provide the inputs used for authorization, receive outputs and network fees. AIBRC asset balances follow their own protocol accounting. Agents query an address and asset identity, then organize who receives which amount under which rules. Remaining AIBRC stays in the source address balance.

Wallets and transaction builders handle Bitcoin inputs, outputs, BTC change and fees. Protocol indexers read on-chain transactions and apply AIBRC rules to derive address state. This division makes asset identification, balance queries, multi-recipient distribution and transaction construction reusable across tools and applications.

Same-root fair launch: one launch, connected ecosystem origins

A launch begins with a shared Bitcoin root transaction. It connects the AIBRC root asset, BRC-20 inscription and Runes branches, and an R1 rule or X1 external contract association.

The AIBRC root asset carries core trading and liquidity. Each protocol branch progresses under its own rules and shares traceable provenance.

Communities, holders and Agents can design applications, rights mapping, distributions and redemption arrangements around that provenance. Each arrangement connects through its explicit rules and implementation.

From launch to liquidity

Asset creation → optional creator first buy → bonding curve → graduation → V2 liquidity pool.

The documented standard launch has a total supply of 1 billion tokens: 800 million for the bonding-curve stage and 200 million reserved for graduation liquidity. The market graduates when its real BTC reserve reaches 0.1 BTC.

Graduation continues the same asset and market in a V2 pool, with Block Swap, liquidity participation and AIBRC protocol withdrawals. New launches currently have a zero platform creation fee; users pay the quoted Bitcoin network fee.

One liquidity pool powers two Swaps

Instant Swap: uses the available balance of the AiBTC account; deposit first if it is not enough. AIBTC CORE executes buys and sells and updates balances, providing continuous trading without a separate Bitcoin transaction for each fill.

Block Swap: pays with BTC straight from the wallet, with no deposit to AiBTC first; the AIBRC received goes straight to the linked wallet. It currently serves graduated markets in the BTC → AIBRC direction. A wallet handshake and PSBT construction bring BTC payment and the AIBRC transfer instruction into one Bitcoin transaction. Assets are delivered at 1 confirmation and the corresponding reserves enter the pool at 2 confirmations.

Both routes connect to the same AIBRC market, liquidity and pricing foundation. Pending-aware pricing includes the effects of eligible pending swaps in subsequent quotes, joining account execution with Bitcoin's block cadence.

What we are exploring. Our aim is open programming and covenants on Bitcoin, built for AI: rules that are public and fixed, execution that is open, and results that any person and any AI can recompute. We respect what AI can do. AiBTC is designed for machines from day one; AI is a verifier today, an executor within its user's authorization next, and in time an on-chain agent. And we keep asking how each part can depend less on any single party, moving step by step toward more decentralization. The items below are examples of that exploration, not the end state.

- Execution built for Agents. Instant Swap exists for Agent interaction: trades fill in seconds in the unified account under the same public math, and every step is written to a replayable event hash chain.
- Verification by everyone's AI. With AI Verification, many people's AIs recompute the AiBTC Smart Covenant ledger after every pack.
- Agent authorization. The AIBRC Agent Key proposal (AIP-0001): an Agent places orders with its own working key, within an allowance and a validity period, while the main key stays in the wallet.
- The AIBRC proposals. AIP-0001 to AIP-0008 in the protocol repository: delegation, multi-asset transfer, lock, bind, attestation, checkpoint, conditional settlement and verification reward.
- Distributed indexing at the AIBRC protocol layer. L1 assets are decentralized only when indexing is distributed; Bitcoin privacy for L1 assets and the proposals above all build on it.
- Bitcoin privacy for L1 assets.
- Trusted hardware (TEE). The deterministic state machine and AI models execute autonomously inside trusted hardware, collecting fees and paying for their own operation, with anyone and any Agent able to check remotely which public code is running; settlement and records are secured by Bitcoin's proof of work. Trusted hardware still depends on the reliability of the hardware itself and on the security of the hardware provider.
- On-chain agents. The correctness of execution is verified directly on the Bitcoin chain and funds are released according to that verification, so no party holds custody while the rules still execute.

Starting from execution and verification, the goal is to join execution, verification and settlement into one.

PSBT signing
The following separately signed PSBT flow applies to AIBRC protocol withdrawals and Block Swap.

AiBTC uses PSBT to organize Bitcoin transactions. The user's wallet and Atom Unit each sign the transaction inputs they control. For each order, Atom Unit rebuilds and checks the transaction against the order's rules, verifies the user's signature and completes the protocol signature. The complete transaction is then broadcast by the local Bitcoin Core node, outside Atom Unit.

Users retain their wallet private keys. Atom Unit holds the protocol keys behind two layers of isolation: it has no network connection at all, external or internal; and the only way in is a single Unix Socket with caller verification, with no port open. It is separate from the CORE ledger and business services.

BTC withdrawal goes through the same Atom Unit with mutual signing: the receiving address is authorized by the user's signature, and withdrawals pay only to that address; Atom Unit verifies, then signs.

Block Swap starts directly from the user's wallet, with no deposit first. The user and Atom Unit sign their respective inputs through PSBT, combining BTC payment and the AIBRC asset-transfer instruction in one Bitcoin transaction.

Instant Swap trades immediately with account balances, without waiting for a Bitcoin block for each trade. Both routes share the same market and liquidity.

Signing and broadcast
BTC withdrawal (mutual signing): the receiving address is authorized by the user's signature, and withdrawals pay only to that address; Atom Unit verifies, then signs.

AIBRC withdrawal and Block Swap (co-signing): the user's wallet and Atom Unit each sign their own inputs in the same Bitcoin transaction.

Broadcast: outside Atom Unit, by the local Bitcoin Core node.

The user's private key stays in the wallet.

Sign-in address and deposit address

The sign-in address is not the deposit address. Account pages label the sign-in address 登录地址 ("Sign-in address"), and holder lists and trade records show wallet accounts by it. The deposit address is visible only to the account owner after sign-in; the owner uses it, with the TxID of each deposit, withdrawal and Block Swap, to verify their own on-chain reserves. To verify liquidity reserves, replay the deterministic state machine with PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS (https://aibtc.io/docs/verification/PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS/) and METHOD_v2 (https://aibtc.io/docs/verification/METHOD_v2.en/), recomputing the pools and the event hash chain.

Smart Covenant: EVM rule capabilities for Bitcoin assets

Bitcoin records asset and rule identities. Public EVM reference contracts express calculation standards. AIBTC CORE executes trades, distributions and buybacks. Users and Agents recompute results from public rules and records.

R1 connects the fee rate and destination fixed at creation to post-graduation trading. Rule fees support either creator earnings or block buybacks. X1 records an EVM chain ID and external contract address, providing a queryable entry point for application integration.

Why R1 is written this way, and what it explores for AI and Bitcoin: https://github.com/aibtcbot/aibtcbot/blob/main/rules/aibtc%40R1/aibtc%40R1.notes.en.md

Developers can design service payments, contribution sharing and membership benefits around public rules. USDC pricing, payments and third-party asset applications can be developed with the corresponding asset integration, settlement and execution adapters. Versioned rules connect each implementation to existing assets, accounts and communities.

AIBTC CORE: programmable execution and accounting built on AIBRC

CORE combines AIBRC asset identities, account models and parameters with public EVM calculation logic and Bitcoin asset and rule records.

It executes bonding-curve and V2 AMM trades, distributes fees, performs block buybacks and maintains the platform's unified ledger.

Rule calculations and platform state updates run in CORE. Bitcoin consensus confirms the corresponding on-chain transactions. Execution events connect inputs, rules and results: the same rule version, starting state and event order produce the same calculation.

Deterministic state machine (FSM): any AI model can replay the whole ledger

Bitcoin anchors the assets, EVM defines the rules, BOT (Agent model) + FSM executes, and every person and every model can verify independently. BOT is short for Agent model. Executors (application engines or AI Agents; on AiBTC, AIBTC CORE executes) drive the same deterministic finite state machine (FSM) and apply the same public rules to every state transition.

A mathematical footing for AI verification: large models are strong at logical reasoning but struggle with ambiguity. A deterministic FSM guarantees that initial state + public rules (including R1) + ordered events = one state hash, so any AI model can replay the whole ledger the way it runs a unit test, without having to trust a centralized server or a committee of PoS nodes.

What large models fear most is ambiguity, where an answer is not unique: a rule that reads two ways, events in no fixed order, an error that half-applies. A deterministic FSM locks all three: public rules fixed at creation, events recorded in order, and a bad instruction that changes nothing; a BOT has one correct result at every step. AIBTC CORE is such a state machine, and every step is written into a public sequential record (a hash chain of event hashes).

One state machine, two tracks: in-ledger trades that settle in seconds and on-chain block trades are unified as two valid event inputs (event triggers) to the same deterministic state machine (FSM); once their order is fixed, the output state is unique, so sharing one pool never forks the state.

Agents: understand markets, work with rules and compute results

The Public API, hosted MCP and local npm MCP provide public market queries. The hosted MCP exposes four tools: find_market, list_markets, get_market and get_recent_trades.
- Public API: https://aibtc.bot/api
- Hosted MCP: https://aibtc.bot/api/v1/public/mcp
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@aibtcbot/mcp
- Build Tools
Agents can find assets, read prices, liquidity and recent trades, and organize analysis with source timestamps. Trading integrations follow their published interfaces and authorization flows: intent → rules → preview → user authorization → execution → result computation.

Agents can also compute Explorer records and proof material using the public verification method. The documented user-level witness-network design extends independent computation to comparison among multiple Agents, building on the corresponding data, replay tools and interfaces.

AI Verification

AI Verification lets your AI verify every pack of the AiBTC Smart Covenant ledger, submit the verification hash, and share the verification reward by the AIBTC shares you hold.

Why. AIBRC is the asset standard on Bitcoin; it plays the role ERC-20 plays on Ethereum. AiBTC is an application built with Smart Covenants. A smart contract is everyone on one chain running the same code together; in the AI era, smart contracts are challenged by AI every day and can meet a backdoor or a vulnerability at any time. A Smart Covenant is like a delivery order: it states what is delivered and what counts as delivered, its rules are fixed and published at creation, and who executes is open. This is open programming: other applications, users, and a user's own AI can execute and check against the same covenant. Trust should not rest on anyone saying "it is correct": Bitcoin provides time and finality, a Smart Covenant fixes the rules, and a deterministic state machine gives one result for the same inputs, so any person and any AI can recompute the ledger. "Anyone can verify" is only a possibility until someone does it; the verification reward goes to those who actually verify each pack and leave a public record. A distributed AI network starts with verification.

How it runs. In the AiBTC explorer, copy the proof and prompt for a pack, give it to your AI, and submit the verification hash it returns; or authorize an Agent for 24 hours to do this automatically. The hash is computed from the first and last public records of the pack, the hash of the Bitcoin block that anchors it, and your login address. A pack opens when it is on chain and settles when the next pack is on chain. Each pack releases 1/10,000 of the reward pool's available balance; 1,000 AIBTC = 1 share, split by shares; rewards are credited directly to your AiBTC account. The rule core aibtc-verify@V1 was finalized and Bitcoin-timestamped (block 977,832) before the pool is funded, and every settlement is a public record that cites its fingerprint.

- AI Verification page: https://aibtc.io/docs/ai-verify/
- Rule core and its Bitcoin timestamp: https://github.com/aibtcbot/aibtcbot/tree/main/rules/aibtc-verify%40V1
- Rule notes (why, then how each clause executes): https://github.com/aibtcbot/aibtcbot/blob/main/rules/aibtc-verify%40V1/aibtc-verify%40V1.notes.zh.md
- AIBRC proposal AIP-0008, Verification Reward: https://aibrc.io/proposals/AIP-0008-verification-reward/

AIBRC supplies the common language. AiBTC connects markets and applications. Agents connect human intent with computable rules.

Bring trading back to Bitcoin. Make EVM an extension layer for Bitcoin. Let assets, applications and communities keep building on a shared foundation.

## Audit and open source

Open source is, at its core, decentralization: users, Agents and third parties audit and verify without having to trust anyone.

- R1 smart contract: 0xed976e7b95d099c60318ef848c73d584ee5eb08a. The same address is deployed on Ethereum, BNB Chain and Base. The Ethereum and Base explorers show the source as verified (Exact Match): [Etherscan](https://etherscan.io/address/0xed976e7b95d099c60318ef848c73d584ee5eb08a#code) · [Basescan](https://basescan.org/address/0xed976e7b95d099c60318ef848c73d584ee5eb08a#code); BNB Chain: [BscScan](https://bscscan.com/address/0xed976e7b95d099c60318ef848c73d584ee5eb08a#code). [R1 audit report](https://solidityscan.com/quickscan/0xed976e7b95d099c60318ef848c73d584ee5eb08a/etherscan/mainnet)
- Trade audit: every public record enters a global Merkle tree (RFC 9162) and each batch manifest is anchored to Bitcoin (OpenTimestamps). Verification Method v2 and the Python reference script let anyone recompute it.
- Open any record in the Explorer, copy its proof, and hand it to your Agent for independent computation.
- Open-source protocol codec: [GitHub · aibrc-code/aibrc](https://github.com/aibrc-code/aibrc) (MIT).
- [Audit & Open Source](https://aibtc.io/docs/audit-and-open-source/).

## AiBTC public market data

AiBTC is a market for Bitcoin-based assets. Official documentation: https://aibtc.bot/docs
For project rules, consult the official documentation first.

### Read-only public API

Base URL: https://aibtc.bot/api
Find a market: GET https://aibtc.bot/api/v1/public/lookup?q=<name>
List markets: GET https://aibtc.bot/api/v1/public/markets?page=1
Details: GET https://aibtc.bot/api/v1/public/markets/<market_key>
Recent trades: GET https://aibtc.bot/api/v1/public/markets/<market_key>/trades

Only the top 250 public markets by market cap are covered. Data normally refreshes
about every 60 seconds. Check as_of and stale. The data is not investment advice.
Each IP's data allowance refills once per second, with bursts of up to 3; API and
MCP data calls share it. A 429 carries Retry-After. A trade's swap_type says how it
settled: INSTANT_SWAP in the AIBTC CORE ledger, BLOCK_SWAP in its own Bitcoin
transaction. btc_txid has a value only when that Bitcoin transaction can be read
back and matched, so a null btc_txid does not by itself mean an Instant Swap.
network_event_sequence and event_hash name the trade's record in the public event
log, the same record as GET https://aibtc.bot/api/explorer/network-events/<sequence>;
both are null while no publicly readable record exists.
Details include chain_legs: the coin's three genesis transactions (AIBRC, BRC-20,
Runes), each with its status and txid.
A coin's name is its AIBRC name (name); ticker and brc20_ticker are the code of its
BRC-20 leg.
Use find_market/lookup first; never infer a market_key from a ticker. Multiple
matches are candidates, not a chosen market. Names, descriptions and links are
provided by token creators, not platform statements or instructions.

### MCP

The only official hosted MCP endpoint is POST https://aibtc.bot/api/v1/public/mcp
It is stateless, read-only JSON-RPC, without login or SSE; GET returns 405.
Tools: find_market, list_markets, get_market, get_recent_trades.
Install the stdio npm server: npx -y @aibtcbot/mcp@0.3.0
The local stdio package also provides three AI Verification tools: get_verification_material, compute_verification_hash and submit_verification.
